items.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022
items.q: So I think he was like a friend even though we never met him. I had never heard him play.

ctx.x: Um hum. The idea of hearing — you were born in ’45 — maybe 1955 there is so much going on in the jazz world, was there an AHA moment for you that — a person or an LP that really propelled you into the career?

Well that’s a good question. Like I said, my father was a semi-professional pianist, very good songwriter/singer, knew a lot of musicians in Philly and there were jam sessions at the house. And the level was really pretty damn high. He had a great record collection. By luck our next door neighbor was a fine tenor player and his sister was a good jazz singer, and people would come over generally. There was a very good trumpet player named Bobby Mojica who had a good career in Detroit as a trumpet player, also was…
get interested in other things because it seemed like the music life so to speak was rather up and down.
